learn.hook: Stone steps, a river, an old fort and the clack-clack of looms. Welcome to Maheshwar!
points: The lesson 'Maheshwar' takes us to a town of rivers, forts and weaving.
Maheshwar is a town in Madhya Pradesh, on the banks of the river Narmada.
Ghats are wide steps that lead down to a river.
Rani Ahilyabai Holkar, a queen of the Holkar family, made Maheshwar her capital more than 250 years ago. The Ahilya Fort stands above the ghats.
The Narmada flows towards the west and falls into the Arabian Sea.

example.q: Read: Maheshwar is a small town in Madhya Pradesh, on the banks of the river Narmada. Long stone steps called ghats lead down to the water. Above the ghats stands the old Ahilya Fort. In many homes, you can hear the clack-clack of handlooms. Weavers make the famous Maheshwari sarees there, thread by thread. Question: Name two things you can see near the river in Maheshwar.
steps: Find the lines about the river.
'Long stone steps called ghats lead down to the water.'
'Above the ghats stands the old Ahilya Fort.'
example.answer: The ghats and the Ahilya Fort.

learn.reallife: Many Indian towns grew up on river banks, like Varanasi on the Ganga and Maheshwar on the Narmada.

games.title: Maheshwar: true or false?
items: Maheshwar is in Madhya Pradesh.
It is a town in Madhya Pradesh.
Maheshwar is on the banks of the river Narmada.
The town is on the Narmada.
Ghats are boats used on the river.
Ghats are steps that lead down to a river.
Maheshwar is famous for its handloom sarees.
Maheshwari sarees are woven there.
The Narmada flows into the Bay of Bengal.
The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea.

games.title: Words from the town
pairs: steps leading down to a river
a strong old building with thick walls
the land along the side of a river
a person who makes cloth on a loom
a place bigger than a village but smaller than a city

quiz.q: In which state is Maheshwar?
quiz.explain: Maheshwar is in Madhya Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without reading

quiz.q: Maheshwar is on the banks of which river?
quiz.explain: Maheshwar is on the Narmada.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rivers of India

quiz.q: Passage line: "Long stone steps called ghats lead down to the water." What are ghats?
options: Steps leading down to the river
quiz.explain: The line tells us ghats are stone steps that lead to the water.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the explanation in the line

quiz.q: Passage line: "Above the ghats stands the old Ahilya Fort." What stands above the ghats?
quiz.explain: The passage says the Ahilya Fort stands above the ghats.
quiz.mistake: Does not find the line

quiz.q: Which queen made Maheshwar her capital?
quiz.explain: Rani Ahilyabai Holkar ruled from Maheshwar. The fort is named after her.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous queens of India

quiz.q: Passage line: "You can hear the clack-clack of handlooms." Which is the sound word?
quiz.explain: 'Clack-clack' copies the sound a loom makes.
quiz.mistake: Picks the name of the thing instead of its sound

quiz.q: Into which sea does the Narmada flow?
quiz.explain: The Narmada flows west and falls into the Arabian Sea.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all big Indian rivers flow east

quiz.q: In "on the banks of the river", what does 'banks' mean?
options: The land along the sides of a river
quiz.explain: 'Bank' has more than one meaning. Next to a river, it means the land at its side.
quiz.mistake: Uses the money meaning of 'bank'

teach.ask: Gappu is flying to Maheshwar. What will Gappu find there?
teach.praise: Wonderful! Maheshwar is in Madhya Pradesh on the Narmada, with ghats, the Ahilya Fort and weavers making sarees. Have a nice trip, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Which river is Maheshwar on? What do people make there?

learn.hook: Thread by thread, row by row, a beautiful saree grows on the loom!
points: A handloom is a loom worked by the weaver's hands and feet, without electricity.
The long threads on a loom are the warp. The threads that go across are the weft.
A shuttle carries the weft thread across the loom.
Maheshwari sarees are light sarees of cotton and silk. They are known for a border that can be worn on either side.
Heritage means the buildings, crafts, songs and ways of life from the past that we value and pass on. National Handloom Day is on 7 August.

example.q: Think it through: why is weaving in Maheshwar called 'heritage'?
steps: Weavers have woven sarees there for a very long time.
The skill is passed down from older weavers to younger ones.
Things from the past that we value and pass on are our heritage.
example.answer: Because it is an old craft that people value and pass on from one generation to the next.

learn.reallife: Ask at home: is there an old saree, shawl or dhoti in your family that was woven by hand? That is heritage in your cupboard!

games.title: How cloth is woven
games.prompt: Put the steps of weaving in order
items: Dye the threads in bright colours
Set the long warp threads on the loom
Pass the shuttle with the weft thread across
Press the thread tight
Repeat row by row until the cloth is ready

quiz.q: What is a handloom?
quiz.explain: A handloom is worked by the weaver's hands and feet, without electricity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all looms are machines

quiz.q: Maheshwari sarees are made in which town?
quiz.explain: They are named after the town of Maheshwar.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the name of the saree with the town

quiz.q: What does 'heritage' mean?
options: Things from the past that we value and pass on
quiz.explain: Heritage is what we get from the past and want to keep for the future.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'heritage'

quiz.q: A person who weaves cloth is called a ___.
quiz.explain: A weaver makes cloth. A tailor stitches clothes from cloth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the weaver and the tailor

quiz.q: Which tool carries the weft thread across the loom?
quiz.explain: The shuttle moves across the loom carrying the weft thread.
quiz.mistake: Thinks weaving is done with a needle

quiz.q: When is National Handloom Day?
quiz.explain: National Handloom Day is on 7 August.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with other national days

quiz.q: Why should we support handloom crafts?
options: They are part of our heritage and give weavers work
quiz.explain: Buying handloom keeps the old craft alive and helps weavers earn.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the value of crafts

quiz.q: Which of these words is made by joining two smaller words?
quiz.explain: hand + loom = handloom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any long word is a compound word

teach.ask: Gappu found a saree with a lovely border. Gappu asks: what is a handloom, and why is it part of our heritage?
teach.praise: Beautiful! A handloom is worked by hand, and weaving is an old skill passed on for a long time. That is our heritage! Gappu is proud.
teach.nudge: How is a handloom worked? Why do we call an old craft our heritage?

learn.hook: maheshwar or Maheshwar? narmada or Narmada? Capital letters help special names stand tall!
points: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
Names of people, places, rivers, days and months begin with a capital letter: Ahilyabai, Maheshwar, Narmada, Monday, August.
The word 'I' is always a capital letter.
Names of seasons (winter, monsoon) do not need a capital letter unless they start a sentence.
Use commas to separate things in a list: We saw ghats, a fort and a loom. Also use a comma after 'Yes' or 'No' at the start: Yes, I can.

example.q: Think it through: correct this sentence: 'in august, meena saw cotton silk and gold thread in maheshwar.'
steps: Start the sentence with a capital: In.
Names of months, people and places need capitals: August, Meena, Maheshwar.
Put a comma between list items: cotton, silk and gold thread.
example.answer: In August, Meena saw cotton, silk and gold thread in Maheshwar.

learn.reallife: When you write your address on a letter or a parcel, the names of your street, city and state all need capital letters.

games.title: Capital letter or not?
buckets: Does not need a capital letter
items: Maheshwar
Narmada
Monday
August
Ahilyabai
river
saree
town
winter

games.title: Capitals and commas: true or false?
items: The word 'I' is always written as a capital letter.
We write 'I', never 'i'.
Names of months begin with a capital letter.
We write January, August and so on.
We put commas between the things in a list.
Example: pens, pencils and erasers.
Every word in a sentence starts with a capital letter.
Only the first word and special names need capitals.
The name of a river, like Narmada, starts with a small letter.
A river's name is a proper noun. It needs a capital letter.

quiz.q: In "We took a boat on the narmada.", which word needs a capital letter?
quiz.explain: Narmada is the name of a river, so it needs a capital N.
quiz.mistake: Thinks common words need capitals

quiz.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: We bought cotton, silk and thread.
We bought cotton silk and thread.
We bought, cotton, silk and thread.
We, bought cotton silk and thread.
quiz.explain: Commas go between the items of a list: cotton, silk and thread.
quiz.mistake: Puts commas in the wrong places or leaves them out

quiz.q: Which of these words should always begin with a capital letter?
quiz.explain: Days of the week are special names, so they always need a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any noun needs a capital

quiz.q: Where should the comma go? "Yes I would like to visit Maheshwar."
quiz.explain: We put a comma after 'Yes' at the start: Yes, I would like to visit Maheshwar.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the comma rule for yes and no

quiz.q: Why does 'Ahilyabai' begin with a capital letter?
options: It is the name of a person
quiz.explain: Names of people are proper nouns and need a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks long words need capitals

quiz.q: Which list is written correctly?
quiz.explain: We put a comma between list items, and 'and' before the last one.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out commas or adds too many

quiz.q: Which word does NOT need a capital letter in the middle of a sentence?
quiz.explain: Seasons like winter are not special names, so they do not need a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks seasons are like months and days

quiz.q: Find the mistake: "My friend ravi lives in Indore."
quiz.explain: Ravi is a person's name, so it needs a capital R.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the small letter in the name

teach.ask: Gappu wrote: 'on monday i flew to maheshwar.' What is wrong? Help Gappu fix it.
teach.praise: Super! 'On Monday I flew to Maheshwar.' The first word, days, places and 'I' need capital letters. Gappu's writing shines!
teach.nudge: Which words in Gappu's sentence need capital letters?
